newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Human rights lawyers yesterday called for a civil disobedience campaign against the national government's identification system which they call a "nightmare." (INQUIRER/CHRONICLE/TIMES)

- The House ethics committee recommended yesterday the suspension for 60 days of Zamboanga del Norte Representative Romeo Jalosjos who has gone into hiding to evade arrest for charges of raping an 11-year old girl last year. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Fuel prices are expected to go up by an average of 22 centavos per litre in the next few days due to the rising prices in the international market, according to sources at the Energy Regulatory Board. (INQUIRER)
- The peso skidded to a 27-month low yesterday but officials and dealers said the fall was temporary and did not reflect economic fundamentals. (BULLETIN)
- The Philippine Stock Exchange kicked off yesterday the operations of the Philippine Central Depository Inc, signalling the start of scripless trading of stocks. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Manila Electric Co may have to shave off 2.0 billion pesos from its budgeted 6.0 billion-peso capital expenditure this year to be able to pay off the higher wages demanded by employees. (MALAYA/CHRONICLE)
